title: The Third Letter of John Timeline
sub: Three Men · Hospitality, Ambition, and a Good Name
desc: John's most personal letter, built around three named individuals — Gaius commended for hospitality, Diotrephes condemned for craving preeminence, and Demetrius praised with a good report from everyone.

eras.label: Era One · 3 John 1
eras.name: Three Men — Hospitality, Ambition, and a Good Name
eras.dates: John's most personal surviving letter, built almost entirely around three named individuals: one praised for hospitality, one condemned for pride, one commended in closing

events.title: Greeting to Gaius — Walking in Truth
events.detail: The elder writes to a specific individual, Gaius, expressing no greater joy than hearing his spiritual children are walking in the truth — a warm, entirely personal opening unlike any of John's other letters.

verses.text: “I have no greater joy than this, to hear that my children are walking in the truth.”

events.title: Gaius's Hospitality to Traveling Missionaries
events.detail: Gaius is commended for supporting traveling gospel workers who accepted nothing from outsiders — John urges continued hospitality, framing financial support as genuine partnership in their work.

verses.text: “We ought to support such men, so that we may be fellow workers with the truth.”

events.title: Diotrephes — Loving to Be First
events.detail: A rare, direct naming of a specific troublemaker: Diotrephes, who craves preeminence in the church, refuses to acknowledge John's authority, spreads malicious gossip, and even expels members who welcome traveling believers.

verses.text: “Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, does not welcome what we say… he himself does not welcome the brothers either, and he forbids those who want to do so and puts them out of the church.”

events.title: Demetrius's Good Witness — Closing
events.detail: In contrast to Diotrephes, Demetrius receives a good report from everyone, including from the truth itself — and John closes, like his second letter, preferring to say the rest face to face rather than with pen and ink.

verses.text: “Do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. The one who does good is of God; the one who does evil has not seen God.”
“Peace to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.” — a verse present in the Greek text but merged into v14 in some English versifications.
